comparison.objective: Candidate adjusts a gripper opening stop, locks its setting, and verifies retained motion; PR-2018 installs a two-sided door lever set while keeping it level as two screws are driven.
comparison.physical_skill: Both involve bimanual stabilization during fastening, but the candidate requires simultaneous driver-and-wrench differential countertorque on a coupled screw/jam nut; PR-2018 supports an external lever orientation while sequentially driving mounting screws after spindle/post insertion.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires a released 90° setting, seated retained nuts, ≤2° drift over three cycles, tool withdrawal, and clearance dwell; PR-2018 requires inserted and seated lever halves, snug screws, and ≤1° level alignment after release.
comparison.reason: The shared counterholding primitive does not erase the different tested mechanism: preserving a threaded stop setpoint against concentric locknut reaction and proving cyclic retention versus holding a door lever level while mounting it. Both records provide concrete numeric success and failure criteria; no material rubric detail is missing.

review_notes: Lever-set assembly: counterhold outsidelever level while two screws driven. Compare two-hand torque stabilization versus coupled adjuster setpoint; no automatic distinct.
